Hi Alicia — great questions and thanks for the snapshot.

Quick answers up front:
- Model shortlist (first pass): Vicuna-13B-Quantized (low-cost baseline), Redwood-RT-Medium (balanced latency/quality), LlamaX-70B-8bit (high-quality for edge cases).
- Conservative token calc: (350,000 requests) * (120 request tokens + 250 response tokens) = ~131.5M tokens/month. Add 20% buffer for retries/diagnostics => ~158M tokens/month.
- Context strategy: propose two context buckets: "compact" (3 most recent turns, ~1–2k context) and "expanded" (full thread up to 8k when we need full history). Start with compact routing to the lower-cost variant and route fallbacks (expanded) to the higher-quality variant when heuristics detect escalation.

I copied Ben and Monica to help with throughput profile and rollout plan. Monica — can you confirm expected QPS and recommended batching policy given 158M tokens/mo and typical 95th percentile latency target of 400ms?

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick throughput sketch:

Baseline assumptions from Alicia's snapshot: peak concurrent requests ~ 1.4k QPS sustained for short bursts; average request/response token sizes match Tessa's calc.

Sizing guidance:
- For compact bucket (3-turn, ~1.5k tokens/query): plan for Redwood-RT-Medium at 12 GPUs for steady-state to meet 95th pct 400ms with continuous batching (batch target 40 ms).
- For expanded bucket (up to 8k tokens): route to LlamaX-70B-8bit on an autoscaling pool (start 4 GPUs, scale to 16 for spikes) with a separate latency SLO (95th ~1.2s).
- Fallbacks & canaries: keep Vicuna-13B-Quantized warm for lowest-cost routing of template answers and low-risk cases; it can handle most compact requests when cost is prioritized.

Operational notes:
- Recommend KV prefix caching for conversation starts (first user turn + system prompt) — expect ~18% token reduction on average.
- Enable dynamic batching with per-model batch caps; prioritize low-latency traffic on dedicated lanes.

Attachments: I exported a quick capacity table (.xlsx) and included example batching profiles.

-ben

Alicia / Tessa —

I ran a short cost/latency simulation using two operating modes (compact-first vs always-expanded). Top-level results:

- Compact-first (route 85% to compact models, 15% to expanded): ~monthly token consumption 142M (post-cache) with estimated monthly inference spend ~$12.6k on Redwood Hosted tiers. Median latency 210ms; 95th 430ms.
- Always-expanded: ~monthly token consumption 238M; median 410ms; 95th 1.1s; estimated spend ~$20.8k.

Recommendation: start with compact-first routing + KV prefix caching + adaptive escalation rules based on negative sentiment/longer thread length. Plan a 6-week uplift test where we open the expanded bucket to 25% to validate quality delta on escalations.

Proposed next steps:
1) Alicia: share any fixed contractual ceilings for monthly spend or committed tokens.
2) Tessa/Ben: prepare canary config and a lightweight A/B eval harness (we'll use the Drive link above).
3) Schedule implementation kickoff (30–45m) next Tue or Wed — Alicia, what time zones work?

—Monica
